title: Who says it? and longer texts

blurb.en: Match each idea to the right child, then read longer articles for facts and feelings.
blurb.vi: Nối mỗi ý với đúng bạn nhỏ, rồi đọc bài viết dài hơn để tìm thông tin và cảm xúc.

article.def: A piece of writing about real people or events, in a magazine or newspaper.
article.ex: We read an *article* about a boy and his tree house.

title.def: The name of a text. It is at the top and tells you the topic.
title.ex: The *title* of the story is 'A cleaner beach'.

paragraph.def: A short part of a text. It starts on a new line and has one main idea.
paragraph.ex: The answer to question 3 is in the third *paragraph*.

quotation.def: The exact words a person said. They are inside speech marks.
quotation.ex: "I was really proud," said Lan. This *quotation* shows her feelings.

same meaning.def: Two sentences that use different words but say the same idea.
same meaning.ex: 'I hardly ever see stars' and 'I almost never see stars' have the *same meaning*.

key word.def: An important word in the question. It helps you find the answer.
key word.ex: In 'Who is careful?', the *key word* is 'careful'.

detail.def: A small piece of information, like a time, a place or a number.
detail.ex: Check every *detail*: they went to the market on Friday evening.

trap.def: A wrong answer that looks right because it uses words from the text.
trap.ex: Daisy says 'rain', but she doesn't like it. That option is a *trap*.

feelings.def: How someone feels: for example happy, nervous, proud or disappointed.
feelings.ex: Read what Jamal did to find his *feelings*.

opinion.def: What a person thinks about something. Look for 'I think' or 'I love'.
opinion.ex: Adam's *opinion* is that teamwork is better than winning.

reason.def: Why something happens. It often comes after 'because' or before 'so'.
reason.ex: The *reason* is that the floor is small.

surprised.def: How you feel when something happens that you didn't expect.
surprised.ex: Jamal was *surprised* that the moon changes so much.

predict.def: To say what will probably happen next, using clues in the text.
predict.ex: Can you *predict* what the class will do next month?

scenes.head: Part 5: two children talk about cold weather
scenes.html:
Poppy
My grandma's village is *freezing* in winter. *I love* wearing my wool hat and gloves there!

Adam
It was *cold* at football yesterday. My hands hurt, and *I wanted to go home*.

steps.en: The question is: *Who enjoys cold weather?* The key word is *enjoys*.
steps.vi: Câu hỏi là: *Ai thích thời tiết lạnh?* Từ khóa là *enjoys* (thích).

steps.en: Adam says *cold*. But he *wanted to go home*. He did not enjoy it.
steps.vi: Adam nói *cold* (lạnh). Nhưng bạn ấy *muốn về nhà*. Bạn ấy không thích.

steps.en: Poppy says *freezing*, not cold. But she says *I love* it. So the answer is Poppy.
steps.vi: Poppy nói *freezing* (rất lạnh), không nói cold. Nhưng bạn ấy nói *I love* (mình rất thích). Vậy đáp án là Poppy.

steps.en: Look for the same MEANING, not the same word.
steps.vi: Hãy tìm cùng Ý NGHĨA, không phải cùng một từ.

title.vi: Đọc bài viết theo thứ tự

scenes.head: Part 6: the start of an article
scenes.html:
A kite in the sky

Son loves kites. Last week, he made a kite with his grandpa. *First*, they cut some paper. *Then* they glued it to thin sticks.

On Sunday, Son took the kite to a field near the river. *At first*, it didn't fly, and Son felt *sad*. *Then* the wind came, and the kite went up high. *"It touched the clouds!"* said Son.

steps.en: The *title* tells you the topic: a kite.
steps.vi: *Tiêu đề* cho bạn biết chủ đề: một con diều.

steps.en: *First*, *then* and *at first* show the order. The questions follow the same order.
steps.vi: *First*, *then* và *at first* cho biết thứ tự. Các câu hỏi cũng theo thứ tự đó.

steps.en: The words in speech marks are a *quotation*. They show how Son felt at the end: very happy.
steps.vi: Những từ trong ngoặc kép là *lời trích dẫn*. Chúng cho thấy cảm xúc của Son lúc cuối: rất vui.

title.vi: Điều gì sẽ xảy ra tiếp theo?

scenes.head: Part 6: the end of the article
scenes.html: Now Son *wants to make* a bigger kite. Grandpa *is going to* buy red paper *next weekend*. Son *is already drawing* a dragon for it.

steps.en: *Wants to*, *is going to* and *next weekend* talk about the future.
steps.vi: *Wants to*, *is going to* và *next weekend* nói về tương lai.

steps.en: A question like *What will Son probably do next?* needs these clues.
steps.vi: Câu hỏi như *Son có thể sẽ làm gì tiếp theo?* cần những gợi ý này.

steps.en: Here the answer is: make a bigger kite. Flying the first kite happened before, so it is not 'next'.
steps.vi: Ở đây đáp án là: làm một con diều to hơn. Thả con diều đầu tiên đã xảy ra rồi, nên đó không phải là 'tiếp theo'.

end.en: Well done! You can match meanings, find feelings and predict what happens next.
end.vi: Giỏi lắm! Bạn biết tìm ý giống nhau, tìm cảm xúc và đoán điều xảy ra tiếp theo.

challenge.result: You found the same meaning, the right person, the feelings and what happens next.

v.q: Lan says: 'I help Dad in the kitchen every evening.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: Every day, Lan helps her dad to cook.
Lan's dad cooks once a week.
whys: She says 'every evening', so it is every day, not once a week.
She says 'I help Dad', so she doesn't cook on her own.
v.hint: Find the words for WHO and HOW OFTEN.
v.worked: 'I *help Dad* in the kitchen *every evening*' means she helps him to cook every day.

v.q: Quan says: 'I've already got a book about stars.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: Quan has a book about stars now.
Quan wants to buy a star book.
Quan is writing a book about the stars.
whys: 'Already got' means he has it now, so he doesn't need to buy it.
He has got a book. He doesn't say he is writing one.
v.hint: What does 'already' tell you: now or later?
v.worked: 'I've *already got* a book' means he has it now.

v.q: Kira: 'I swim in the sea.' Tia: 'I dance at the centre.' Jamal: 'I watch the rain from my window.' Who goes into the water?
whys: Tia dances at the centre, not in the water.
Jamal watches the rain from inside. He doesn't go into the water.
v.hint: Rain is water too. Who is IN the water?
v.worked: Kira says '*I swim in the sea*'.

v.q: Ollie: 'My dog runs in the rain.' Daisy: 'My rabbit hides when it thunders.' Quan: 'My fish don't hear the storm.' Who has a pet that gets scared?
whys: Ollie's dog runs in the rain, so it isn't scared.
Quan's fish don't hear the storm, so they aren't scared.
v.hint: What does an animal do when it is scared?
v.worked: Daisy's rabbit '*hides* when it thunders'. Animals hide when they are scared.

v.q: Son: 'At first I didn't want to go to the club, but now I love it.' How does Son feel now?
opts: He really enjoys going to the club.
He is bored at the club.
whys: That was 'at first'. Now his feelings are different.
He says 'I love it', so he isn't bored.
v.hint: Find the word 'now' and read after it.
v.worked: '*Now I love it*' means he enjoys the club.

v.q: Poppy: 'I painted all day, and Grandma put my picture on her wall!' How does Poppy probably feel?
whys: Her '!' shows good news. Nothing in her words sounds bored.
Nothing bad happened, so she isn't angry.
v.hint: What does the '!' tell you? Is it good news or bad news?
v.worked: Grandma put her picture '*on her wall*'. That is good news, so Poppy feels proud.

v.q: Adam: 'We lost today. Next week we're going to practise passing every day.' What will Adam's team do next?
whys: Adam doesn't talk about another match.
They are going to practise, so they aren't stopping.
v.hint: Find 'going to'. It shows the future.
v.worked: 'Next week we're *going to practise passing*.'

v.q: Tia: 'My brother's photos are great. I'd like to try it too.' What will Tia probably do?
whys: Tia talks about photos, not drawing.
She wants to try taking photos herself.
v.hint: What does 'it' mean in 'try it too'?
v.worked: 'I'd like to *try it* too': 'it' means taking photos.

blurb.vi: Tìm câu cùng nghĩa, chọn đúng bạn nhỏ và đọc một bài viết ngắn.

v.q: Son says: 'I hardly ever stay inside when it's sunny.' What does he mean?
opts: He is almost always outside on sunny days.
He stays inside on most sunny days.
He never goes outside when it's sunny.
whys: 'Hardly ever stay inside' means he almost never stays in.
This is the opposite. He goes outside a lot.
v.hint: 'Hardly ever' means almost never. Read the sentence again with 'almost never'.
v.worked: '*Hardly ever* stay inside' = he almost never stays in, so he is outside.

v.q: Tia says: 'I've never been on a plane.' What does she mean?
opts: She has not flown in a plane before.
She went on a plane once last year.
She goes on a plane every holiday.
whys: 'Never' means not one time.
'Never' means not one time, so not every holiday.
v.hint: How many times is 'never'?
v.worked: 'I've *never* been on a plane' = she has not flown before.

v.q: Kira says: 'I'm really keen on surfing.' What does she mean?
opts: She is not good at swimming.
whys: 'Keen on' is a happy word. It doesn't mean afraid.
She doesn't talk about how well she swims.
v.hint: Is 'keen on' a good feeling or a bad feeling?
v.worked: '*Keen on*' means you like something a lot.

v.q: Jamal says: 'Storms don't scare me now.' What does he mean?
opts: He isn't afraid of storms any more.
He was never afraid of storms before.
He is very scared of storms today.
whys: 'Now' tells you he WAS scared before.
This is the opposite: storms don't scare him.
v.hint: What does the word 'now' tell you about before?
v.worked: 'Storms *don't scare me now*' = he isn't afraid any more, but he was before.

v.q: Daisy says: 'Working in the garden is more fun than watching TV.' What does she mean?
opts: She enjoys gardening more than TV.
She enjoys TV more than gardening.
She doesn't like gardening or TV.
whys: This is the other way round. The garden is 'more fun'.
She says gardening is fun.
v.hint: Which thing comes before 'more fun than'?
v.worked: 'Working in the garden is *more fun than* watching TV.'

v.q: Ollie says: 'I'd like a skate park in my street.' What does he mean?
opts: There isn't a skate park near his home.
There is a skate park in his street.
whys: He would like one in his street, so there isn't one there now.
He wants a skate park, so he likes them.
v.hint: 'I'd like' shows something a person wants. What is the problem now?
v.worked: '*I'd like a skate park* in my street' = there isn't one near his home now.

v.q: Who is learning to do something better?
whys: Kira surfs, but she doesn't say she is getting better.
Son's little sister is learning. Son is the teacher!
v.hint: Look for words like 'better' or 'learn'. Who is the learner?
v.worked: Tia says '*I'm getting better* every week'.

v.q: Why did Tia feel sick before the show?
opts: She was very nervous about the show.
whys: The article doesn't say she was ill.
The music helped her. She 'forgot about all the people'.
v.hint: Find 'felt sick' and read to the end of the sentence.
v.worked: 'Tia felt sick *because she was so nervous*.'

stim.head: A short article
stim.html:
Tia's first dance show

Tia has gone to dance class for a year. Last Friday, her class danced in a show at the community centre.

Before the show, Tia felt sick because she was so nervous. But when the music started, she forgot about all the people. Everybody clapped at the end.

"I want to do it again!" said Tia. Her teacher is already planning another show for the summer.

v.q: Why was Kira angry?
opts: Her friends didn't want to surf.
whys: Her friends helped her. They didn't say no.
The article doesn't talk about her surfboard.
v.hint: Find 'angry'. The reason comes after 'because'.
v.worked: 'She was angry, *because plastic is dangerous for sea animals*.'

v.q: Who can do their sport close to home?
whys: Adam's club is 'thirty minutes from my flat by bus'.
The skate park is next to his GRANDMA's house, not his own home.
v.hint: All three say where they go. Check WHOSE home it is near.
v.worked: Kira says '*My family lives next to the sea*, so I can surf after school'.

stim.head: Part 5: three children
stim.html:
Our favourite sports

Adam
I play football for a club every Saturday. The club is at the sports centre in the city. It's thirty minutes from my flat by bus. Next season I'd like to try a new position: goalkeeper! Last month our team lost a big match, and I was very sad. But our coach said, 'You all helped each other.' Now I think playing well together is better than winning.

Kira
Surfing is my favourite sport. My family lives next to the sea, so I can surf after school. I tried swimming and tennis before, but surfing is much more exciting. I fell off my board a lot at first. Now I can stand up for a long time, and I'm not scared of big waves any more. I really want to win a surfing competition one day.

Ollie
I go skateboarding every Sunday. The skate park is next to my grandma's house, so we have lunch with her after. I usually skate alone, and I don't like competitions. I just want to have fun. I can do four tricks now, and I'm learning a new one. Next year I'd like to try rugby with my cousin. It looks really exciting!

v.q: Who would like the weather to be different where they live?
whys: Son loves the rainy season. He doesn't want a change.
Daisy doesn't like the rain much, but she says 'I don't mind'.
v.hint: Find what each child says about the weather at home. Who wants it to change?
v.worked: Poppy's city is hot and humid, and she says '*I'd love some cooler weather at home too*'.

stim.head: Part 5: three children
stim.html:
My favourite weather

Poppy
My favourite weather is cool and windy. My grandma lives in the mountains in the north. In December it's freezing there, and sometimes there's ice on the windows. I wear my thick wool hat, and Grandma makes hot soup for me. Then we paint pictures together. In my city it's always hot and humid. I'd love some cooler weather at home too.

Son
I love the rainy season! The sky goes dark, and then the rain is very heavy. I watch the lightning from my window. My little sister is scared of the thunder, so I sit with her and hold her hand. When the rain stops, I go outside with my friends. We jump in the big puddles. Mum isn't happy about my wet clothes!

Daisy
I like warm, sunny days best, because I can work in the garden with my dad. We grow beans and tomatoes. When it's very hot and dry, we have to water the plants every morning and every evening. I don't like the rainy season much, because it's too wet to go outside. But Dad says the rain is good for our garden, so I don't mind.

v.q: Who would like to play a new sport?
whys: Adam wants a new position, but it is still football.
Kira tried swimming and tennis before. Now she only talks about surfing.
v.hint: Two children use the word 'new' or 'try'. Which one means a new SPORT?
v.worked: Ollie says '*Next year I'd like to try rugby*'. Rugby is a new sport for him.

A home in a tree

They worked on it for three weekends. First, they made a strong floor with wood. Then they built four walls and a roof. The roof is green, so it is hard to see the tree house from the street.

The tree house is small, but it has a little window and a round door. There is a rope ladder to climb up. Grandad says only two people can go in at the same time, because the floor is not very big.

Ollie's favourite thing is the window. He can see birds in the tree, and on clear days he can see the hills far away.

Grandma made some cushions from old wool and cloth. Now Ollie climbs up after skateboarding. He reads comics there and eats mangoes from the tree.

Next summer, Ollie and Grandad want to build a small table inside. "Then I can do my homework up there too," Ollie says.
